primaryText: There is a blue circle on the card.
translation: There is a blue circle on the card.
comment: ⇝ |C| = 1, C the set of blue circles on the card.

primaryText: There are blue circles on the card.
translation: There are blue circles on the card.

primaryText: There isn't any blue circle on the card.
translation: There isn't any blue circle on the card.
comment: ⇝ |C| = 0: under negation the number does not affect truth conditions.

primaryText: There aren't any blue circles on the card.
translation: There aren't any blue circles on the card.

primaryText: There is no blue circle on the card.
translation: There is no blue circle on the card.

primaryText: There are no blue circles on the card.
translation: There are no blue circles on the card.

primaryText: There are two blue circles on the card.
translation: There are two blue circles on the card.
comment: The competitor whose semantics entails at least two witnesses, source of the atomicity inference of (1a) on the scalar account.

primaryText: This book has no table of contents.
translation: This book has no table of contents.
comment: A book can have at most one table of contents: exactly one is conceivable.

primaryText: This book has no tables of contents.
translation: This book has no tables of contents.
comment: More than one table of contents is not conceivable: the plural's conceivability presupposition fails.

primaryText: This book has no chapter.
translation: This book has no chapter.
comment: A book never has a single chapter: the singular's conceivability presupposition fails.

primaryText: This book has no chapters.
translation: This book has no chapters.
comment: Several chapters are conceivable.

primaryText: Do you have children?
translation: Do you have children?
comment: Adapted from Farkas and de Swart (2010): in a prototypical situation a parent has more than one child.

primaryText: Do you have a child?
translation: Do you have a child?
comment: Adapted from Farkas and de Swart (2010).

primaryText: Do you have a child on our baseball team?
translation: Do you have a child on our baseball team?
comment: Adapted from Farkas and de Swart (2010): a parent prototypically has one child on a given team.

primaryText: Do you have children on our baseball team?
translation: Do you have children on our baseball team?
comment: Adapted from Farkas and de Swart (2010).

primaryText: I arrived late at the seminar and all the seats were taken, so I went to have a look in the surrounding rooms, but there was no chair anywhere.
translation: I arrived late at the seminar and all the seats were taken, so I went to have a look in the surrounding rooms, but there was no chair anywhere.
comment: Acceptable and if anything more natural than (12b), although the speaker is more likely to find many chairs than exactly one: what matters is that the speaker needs one chair, so probability is not the right predictor.

primaryText: I arrived late at the seminar and all the seats were taken, so I went to have a look in the surrounding rooms, but there were no chairs anywhere.
translation: I arrived late at the seminar and all the seats were taken, so I went to have a look in the surrounding rooms, but there were no chairs anywhere.
comment: Acceptable.

primaryText: There is no bathroom here. It's upstairs.
translation: There is no bathroom here. It's upstairs.
comment: The example on which DPL makes negation block dynamic binding.

primaryText: There is no bathroom here, or it is upstairs.
translation: There is no bathroom here, or it is upstairs.
comment: A bathroom pronoun in the second disjunct refers back to the negative indefinite of the first.

primaryText: It is false that there is no bathroom here. It is upstairs.
translation: It is false that there is no bathroom here. It is upstairs.
comment: A negated indefinite under negation can be referred back to.

primaryText: There is no bathroom here. It would be downstairs.
translation: There is no bathroom here. It would be downstairs.
comment: Anaphora to a negated indefinite in a modal context.

primaryText: — There is no bathroom here. — Yes there is! It is upstairs.
translation: — There is no bathroom here. — Yes there is! It is upstairs.
comment: Anaphora to a negated indefinite after a denial.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. It's just hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. It's just hard to see.
comment: Felicitous for a card with a unique circle; not natural when the speaker sees several.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. They're just hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. They're just hard to see.
comment: The pronoun's number must match the indefinite's.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. It's just hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. It's just hard to see.
comment: The pronoun's number must match the indefinite's.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. They're just hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. They're just hard to see.
comment: Degraded when the speaker can see that the card has exactly one circle.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. It has several but they're hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have a circle. It has several but they're hard to see.
comment: A new indefinite introduces a referent of the appropriate number: the inference is not present in the first sentence.

primaryText: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. It has one but it's hard to see.
translation: It's not true that the card doesn't have any circles. It has one but it's hard to see.
comment: A new indefinite introduces a referent of the appropriate number.

primaryText: There is no blue circle on the card.
translation: There is no blue circle on the card.
comment: The first speaker's negative assertion, repeated from (3a).

primaryText: Yes there is! It's just hard to see.
translation: Yes there is! It's just hard to see.
context: There are several, hard to see blue circles on the card.
comment: The pronoun's number does not match the referent, or the referent is not maximal.

primaryText: Yes there is! They're just hard to see.
translation: Yes there is! They're just hard to see.
context: There are several, hard to see blue circles on the card.
comment: The pronoun's number does not match that of the indefinite that licenses it; the paper prints 'They're just are to see'.

primaryText: Yes there is! There are several, they're just hard to see.
translation: Yes there is! There are several, they're just hard to see.
context: There are several, hard to see blue circles on the card.
comment: Ineffability resolved by introducing a new referent.

primaryText: Yes, there are several, but they're hard to see.
translation: Yes, there are several, but they're hard to see.
context: There are several blue circles on the card. Q: Is there a blue circle on the card?
comment: The parenthetical 'there are several' is obligatory: without it the plural pronoun has no licensing referent.

primaryText: Yes, but it's hard to see.
translation: Yes, but it's hard to see.
context: There are several blue circles on the card. Q: Is there a blue circle on the card?
comment: The singular pronoun does not fit the several circles: the same ineffability as in (22) arises for indefinites in questions.
